newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares surge higher despite strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares surge higher despite strike.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares surged nearly 52 points to another record high on Monday in a market that shrugged off the start of a strike by local civil servants, mainly doctors and nurses, brokers said.
"The strike had no effect, and unless it continues for a long time it will not have much effect on the share market," one broker said of the strike for higher pay, the second in two months.
"I think there will be some concern, but the outlook is still generally bullish," he added.

Dealers said many local investors were trading on forecasts that agriculture-powered Zimbabwe will have a near-normal rainy season in the farming season starting in November and that its economy will grow by seven percent in 1997, up from an an estimated five percent this year.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's 57-counter industrial index climbed 51.57 points to 7,408.88, boosted by strong trade in a couple of bluechips, including banking group Barclays, 100 cents higher at 2,200, and agricultural equipment manufacturer IHL, which surged 1,100 cents to 6,000.
But the secondary seven-share mining index slipped 0.82 points to close at 1,253.71 following a 10-cent loss in nickel producer Bindura at 1,090.
